dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent, an AI assistant, and our call is recorded for quality. To help me understand what is going on with your right ring finger, could you tell me if you have recently injured it, or if you've had any cuts, punctures, or bites on that hand?
Yeah, I injured it a couple days ago playing football. My finger got caught in another player's jersey and he pulled away really hard. It's been swollen and painful ever since.
That sounds like a classic sports injury. Are you able to bend the very tip of your right ring finger down toward your palm?
No, I can't bend the tip at all. When I try to make a fist, that finger just stays straight while the others curl down. It's really frustrating.

I see. Are you still able to bend the middle joint of that finger, or is that joint also stiff and unable to move? I would also like to order an imaging test to check for any fractures.

REQUEST TEST: Right_Hand_X-Ray
RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand shows no bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.
Could you let me know if you are able to bend the middle joint of that finger, and do you feel any tenderness or a lump further down on the palm side of your hand or finger?
Yeah, I can bend the middle joint okay, it's just the tip that won't move. The pain and tenderness are mostly right at that last joint near the fingertip, not really down in my palm or anything.

Got it. Do you feel any numbness or tingling in that finger, or is the sensation completely normal? I would also like to order an MRI to evaluate the tendon.

REQUEST TEST: Right_Ring_Finger_MRI

RESULTS: MRI of the Right Hand shows disruption of the extensor tendon at the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger, consistent with extensor tendon rupture (mallet finger). No fractures identified. Soft tissue edema present around the DIP joint.
